# sing-box Observability Stack for KernelSU

This standalone ARM64 KernelSU module installs and runs:

- Grafana 13.2.0 on 127.0.0.1:3000;
- Prometheus 3.14.0 on 127.0.0.1:9091;
- the Grafana-signed Prometheus datasource plugin 13.1.7;
- the Grafana-signed Infinity datasource plugin 4.0.0;
- the sing-box dashboard and two automatically provisioned datasources.

All upstream archives are downloaded during module installation and verified
against the pinned SHA-256 values in module/core.conf before extraction.
Persistent state lives in /data/adb/singbox-observability.

## Requirements

- KernelSU and an ARM64 Android device;
- network access during the first installation;
- at least 1.5 GB free space while installing;
- sing-box observability on 127.0.0.1:9090;
- the sing-box API secret, initially configured as singbox.

Grafana is about 406 MiB compressed, Prometheus about 94 MiB, the Grafana
Prometheus datasource about 15 MiB, and Infinity about 15 MiB. Temporary
archives are removed after installation.

## Build

On Linux or WSL, install bash, jq, zip, unzip, curl, and sha256sum, then run:

~~~sh
./scripts/build.sh
./scripts/validate.sh
./scripts/verify-upstream.sh
~~~

The installable output is build/singbox-observability-stack-0.1.3.zip.

## Release from GitHub

The repository workflow builds and publishes a release when a tag matching the
module version is pushed. Update `module.prop`, commit the change, then create
and push the matching tag:

~~~sh
git tag v0.1.3
git push origin main v0.1.3
~~~

The workflow requires the tag to equal `v<version>` from `module.prop`. It runs
all build and validation scripts, verifies pinned upstream hashes, and uploads
the module ZIP together with its SHA-256 file to the GitHub Release. A failed
validation prevents a release from being created.

## Install and first login

Install the ZIP from KernelSU Manager and reboot. Grafana becomes available at
http://127.0.0.1:3000. The username is admin. A random password is printed by
the installer and stored in this root-only file:

~~~text
/data/adb/singbox-observability/grafana-admin-password
~~~

On first install, the default dashboard is provisioned in the sing-box folder
only when the persistent dashboard directory does not already contain JSON
files. Later starts, repairs, and module upgrades do not overwrite user
dashboards. These datasources are created automatically:

| Name | UID | URL |
|------|-----|-----|
| sing-box Prometheus | singbox-prometheus | http://127.0.0.1:9091 |
| sing-box Infinity | singbox-infinity | http://127.0.0.1:9090/observability/v1 |

Infinity sends the sing-box Bearer token from Grafana's backend. The token is
stored in Grafana secure datasource configuration, not in the dashboard JSON.

## Dashboard customization

Grafana stores its database under the persistent state directory, so dashboards
imported in the web UI and edits saved in the web UI survive module restarts,
device reboots, repairs, and upgrades. Use **Dashboards > New > Import** to
upload a dashboard JSON file. Select `sing-box Prometheus` and `sing-box
Infinity` when Grafana asks for datasource mappings.

Root users can also copy JSON files to:

~~~text
/data/adb/singbox-observability/dashboards
~~~

Grafana scans that directory every 30 seconds. A file placed there remains the
authoritative source for its provisioned dashboard; replacing the file updates
the dashboard. File-provisioned dashboards can also be edited in the web UI.
To make one fully UI-managed, remove its JSON file after Grafana has loaded it;
the dashboard remains in Grafana's persistent database. Avoid duplicate
dashboard UIDs across JSON files.

## Configuration

Edit /data/adb/singbox-observability/settings.conf as root, then use the module
Action button with restart or reboot.

~~~ini
GRAFANA_PORT=3000
GRAFANA_LISTEN_ADDR=127.0.0.1
PROMETHEUS_PORT=9091
SINGBOX_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9090/observability/v1
SINGBOX_API_SECRET=singbox
SINGBOX_PROMETHEUS_TARGET=127.0.0.1:9090
SINGBOX_METRICS_PATH=/observability/v1/metrics
PROMETHEUS_SCRAPE_INTERVAL=15s
PROMETHEUS_RETENTION_TIME=30d
PROMETHEUS_RETENTION_SIZE=512MB
MIN_FREE_SPACE_MB=1536
MAX_LOG_SIZE_MB=10
~~~

## Service control

Run these commands from a root shell. The KernelSU Action button performs the
same operation as `restart`.

~~~sh
MODDIR=/data/adb/modules/singbox_observability_stack
"$MODDIR/action.sh" status
"$MODDIR/action.sh" start
"$MODDIR/action.sh" stop
"$MODDIR/action.sh" restart
"$MODDIR/action.sh" repair
~~~

## Trusted LAN access

Grafana remains loopback-only by default. To make only Grafana available on a
trusted LAN, set the following value in
`/data/adb/singbox-observability/settings.conf`, then restart the module:

~~~ini
GRAFANA_LISTEN_ADDR=0.0.0.0
~~~

Connect to `http://PHONE_LAN_IP:3000`. Prometheus and the sing-box API remain
loopback-only. Plain HTTP does not protect the Grafana password or session from
other devices on the LAN, so do not use this setting on public Wi-Fi or create
a router port-forward. Use TLS or a trusted VPN for access outside the LAN.

Prometheus scrapes 127.0.0.1:9090/observability/v1/metrics with the configured
Bearer token. It has both the 30-day retention limit and the 512 MB size limit;
whichever is reached first limits storage.

Do not expose Grafana or Prometheus on 0.0.0.0 without a separate TLS and
authentication design.

## Diagnostics

The Action script supports status, restart, stop, install, and repair. It checks
Prometheus /-/ready, Grafana /api/health, and the authenticated sing-box /status
endpoint.

Logs:

~~~text
/data/adb/singbox-observability/logs/install.log
/data/adb/singbox-observability/logs/prometheus.log
/data/adb/singbox-observability/logs/grafana.log
~~~

Uninstall removes downloaded runtimes but intentionally preserves settings,
credentials, the Grafana database, dashboards, and Prometheus history.

## License and upstream components

The module source and bundled dashboard use the repository `LICENSE`, inherited
from sing-box. Grafana, Prometheus, and Infinity are not redistributed in the
source tree or build ZIP; the module downloads their official release packages,
which remain subject to their respective upstream licenses and notices.
